headline: Turin's next AI agent builder could be you—start shipping agentic workflows before the rest of Politecnico catches on.
why_now: AI Agents is the highest-signal topic in your stack: project_potential (96) and career_value (95) are off the charts, and GitHub activity (96) plus Hugging Face activity (92) show the tooling ecosystem is exploding right now. With job_demand at 85 and news_mentions at 88, employers are already hunting for people who can actually build these systems, not just talk about them.
study: Master the foundations: read 'ReAct' and 'Toolformer' papers, then the LangChain and LlamaIndex docs to understand how agents reason, retrieve, and call tools.
Build a local agent playground in Python using the OpenAI or Hugging Face API plus LangGraph; add tool-calling (web search, calculator, file I/O) and a simple memory module.
Study one multi-agent pattern end-to-end: try CrewAI or AutoGen to coordinate two or three specialized agents on a shared task (e.g., research + write + edit).
Learn the eval side: read about trajectories, success rates, and how to benchmark agents with tools like LangSmith or Phoenix, so your portfolio work looks rigorous.
Browse the top 20 AI-agent repos on GitHub tagged this month and clone+modify two of them to internalize patterns.

build.title: Turin Local AI Agent: a multilingual tourist concierge that plans a Turin itinerary end-to-end
build.description: An agent that takes a tourist's interests, dates, and budget, then autonomously calls tools to check weather, look up opening hours of museums (via APIs or scraping), reserve a slot at Museo Egizio, suggest a Piedmont restaurant, and compose a day-by-day plan in Italian or English. Why it impresses: it combines tool use, multi-step planning, API integration, memory, and a real local angle that makes it memorable to recruiters in Turin and beyond.
stack: OpenAI or open-source model from Hugging Face
SQLite for memory of past trips
deliverables: Public GitHub repo with clean README, architecture diagram, and setup instructions
Live Streamlit demo or short Loom video showing a real Turin itinerary
Technical write-up (Medium or personal blog) explaining agent design choices and what failed

publish: Create a clean GitHub README with screenshots and architecture.
Publish a working demo or notebook.
risks: Tool-use loops can rack up API costs and get stuck in infinite reasoning; cap iterations and set budgets in code.
Agent demos often break under live API changes—pin dependencies and add retries so your portfolio piece stays runnable months from now.
confidence: Recommendation is very strong: every signal supports AI agents as a high-leverage, buildable, and hireable direction for a student in Turin right now.
